pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): top-left caption “A busy day at Dr. Ananya’s clinic.” Below it, a daytime clinic exterior. A doctor in a white coat, teal kurta and stethoscope stands in the doorway and waves in an older woman in a lilac sari, who is seen from behind. Two waiting patients sit on metal chairs at right, also seen from behind. Tier 2 left panel: a receptionist with a long braid, wearing a blue printed kurta, is on a desk phone, writing in a ledger beside a tall stack of books. Patients' heads fill the foreground. Her first balloon, top left: “Appointments, patient details, follow-ups...” Her second balloon, right and slightly lower: “I wish everything were easier to manage!” Both tails point to her. Tier 2 right panel: the doctor stands thinking, hand at chin, with the receptionist still on the phone in the background. Balloon with tail to the doctor: “Our time belongs with patients. Let’s make the rest simpler.”
pages.observation: The order is clear: caption, then the receptionist's two balloons left to right and top to bottom, then the doctor's answer in the right panel. The doctor's line reads as a response to the receptionist's complaint. The caption names Dr. Ananya, and the coat and stethoscope make it clear she is the doctor. The receptionist is not named. The phrase “Our time belongs with patients” is slightly unidiomatic but readable. No lettering covers a face or hand. The receptionist's tails pass close above her head but do not cover it. The doctor's hair is a low bun with loose strands, consistent with panel 1.

pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): top-left caption “The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.” Top-right teal label “WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic”. The doctor types on a laptop showing a setup screen with step dots. The window shows a sunset sky, and a mug sits at right. Tier 2 left panel: the doctor sits thoughtfully at the laptop, finger at her chin. Balloon with tail to her: “We can organise our clinic workflow here.” Tier 2 right panel: the receptionist stands holding a phone with a calendar app. Balloon with tail down to her: “And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.” Lower teal label: “WELBUK CARE for clinic staff”. Tier 3 (wide panel): the doctor at her desk, smiling, with a fist raised. The receptionist stands at right with her phone. Balloon with tail to the doctor: “One team. Better coordination.”
pages.observation: There is an unmarked time change. Page 1 is bright daytime, and this page has an evening/sunset window with no time caption; the onboarding caption only implies a later moment. The reading order in each tier is clear. The receptionist's line “And our team...” follows the doctor's line naturally. In tier 1, the top-right label sits after the caption and reads like product signage, not dialogue. The tier 2 right label “WELBUK CARE for clinic staff” sits over the receptionist's lower dress and near her left hand. It does not cover the phone or her face but crowds her figure. In tier 3, the doctor's hair looks looser and wavier, and the bun is less visible than in tiers 1 and 2. This is a minor hair continuity variation. The doctor's earring and teal kurta are consistent.

pages.scan: Tier 2 left panel: caption “A later morning: patients can always check in at the front desk.” An elderly man with glasses and a cane checks in with the braided receptionist at the front desk. Waiting patients and a QR stand are in the background. Tier 2 right panel: caption “Some check in ahead on the Welbuk Health app.” A young woman with a ponytail, in a coral printed kurta with a navy shoulder bag, taps a phone outside the clinic entrance. Tier 2 left panel: caption “Ravi scans the QR code at the door.” A bearded man in a sage-green shirt with a brown shoulder bag and a wristwatch scans a QR stand with his phone. The receptionist, the elderly man and the woman are visible behind him. Tier 2 right panel: caption “A short form on his own phone, shared with consent.” Close-up of his hands holding the phone, which shows a form with a check mark, next to his face in profile. Tier 3 (wide panel): caption “Every check-in gets a slot on the screen.” A wall screen shows “A-10 · A-11 · A-12”. The elderly man, the young woman and Ravi sit side by side on waiting chairs, looking up at the screen. No balloons.
pages.observation: This page is all captions. The order is clear: top-left, top-right, middle-left, middle-right, bottom. The “later morning” caption marks the time change from page 2's evening. Ravi is named in a caption at first appearance, with no prior introduction. This is acceptable. The two other patients stay unnamed, so it is unclear which slot belongs to whom. The reader may assume Ravi is A-12 only after page 4. In the middle-left panel, the caption box's right edge sits very close to the top of Ravi's hair but does not seem to cover his face. In the top-left panel, the caption covers part of a teal wall screen behind the desk. Clothing and props are consistent across panels: Ravi's sage shirt, brown bag strap and watch; the woman's coral kurta and navy bag; the elderly man's cane. In the bottom panel, Ravi's bag is on his lap.

pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): top-left caption “Soon, his slot comes up.” Ravi stands up from the waiting chairs, bag on his shoulder. A wall screen at top right shows the label “NOW · A-12”. The receptionist is at her desk at right. Tier 2 left panel: caption “A quick vitals check first.” A new character, a nurse with short wavy hair in lavender scrubs with an ID lanyard, takes Ravi's blood pressure with a cuff and pulse oximeter. His bag is on the floor. Balloon with tail to the nurse: “Hi, Ravi! Just relax your arm for me.” Tier 2 right panel: caption “Dr. Ananya is notified when he’s ready.” The doctor holds a tablet with a check icon and the label “RAVI · READY”, smiling.
pages.observation: The order is clear: tier 1 caption, then the screen label, then the left caption and the nurse's balloon, then the right caption and tablet label. Linking “A-12” to Ravi depends on the reader remembering page 3's screen and inferring that A-12 is his. No caption says this, but “his slot comes up” helps. The nurse is introduced without a name or role caption, though her scrubs make the role clear. The “RAVI · READY” label box sits over the tablet screen, close to the doctor's right-hand fingers at the tablet's edge. The fingers stay visible. No lettering covers a face. Ravi's shirt, bag and watch are consistent. The doctor's bun and stethoscope are consistent.

pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): the doctor gestures toward Ravi, who sits relaxed in a consultation chair with his bag beside him. Balloon at top center, with tail to the doctor: “Hello, Ravi. Tell me what brings you in.” Large teal label at left, over her laptop: “PATIENT DETAILS: current vitals · prior health info · allergy panel · AI mic option · patient docs · lab reports”. Tier 2 (wide, long shot): the doctor at left and Ravi at right, with a laptop between them showing a mic and shield icon. Left balloon, tail to the doctor: “May the AI listen and save notes of our talk?” Middle balloon, tail to Ravi: “Yes, I agree.” Right teal label: “AI VOICE CONSENT: asked at the first visit, before any voice is saved”. Tier 3 left panel: Ravi with a hand at his neck, looking a little sheepish. Balloon with tail to him: “I’ve been feeling tired lately.” Lower-left teal label over a laptop with a glowing mic icon: “SOAP NOTES: fill in manually and choose ICD or SNOMED codes, or let AI listen and summarise the conversation”. Tier 3 right panel: caption “Technology supports the workflow. The conversation stays human.” The doctor smiles and listens. Ravi's back-of-head is in the foreground.
pages.observation: The question-and-answer order is interrupted. The doctor asks “Tell me what brings you in.” Before Ravi answers, a whole tier about AI consent intervenes, and only then comes “I’ve been feeling tired lately.” A reader can follow this, but the answer to the first question is delayed, and the consent question could be read as interrupting him. In tier 2, the two balloons are side by side and their tails cross the open space in the correct directions, so the “Yes, I agree.” reply is unlikely to be skipped. The text-heavy labels (PATIENT DETAILS, SOAP NOTES) are long, dense lists. Readers may skim them and lose the dialogue rhythm. The PATIENT DETAILS label fully covers the doctor's laptop screen. The SOAP NOTES label covers the left half of the laptop and part of the panel's lower-left. Neither covers a face or hand. The transition from the vitals station on page 4 to the consultation room has no caption but is easy to understand. Ravi's watch, shirt and bag are consistent.

pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): close-up of a laptop screen. Header label “SPECIALITY-SPECIFIC TREATMENT PLANNER”. Three card labels, read left to right: “Dentist: odontogram”, “Eye doctor: eye markers”, “Paediatrician: growth scales · vaccines”. Each has an icon: a ring of teeth, an eye with markers, and a growth chart with checklist. A hand in a white sleeve with a teal cuff (the doctor's) rests on the trackpad. Tier 2 (large wide panel): the doctor gestures toward Ravi as both smile. Balloon at top, tail to the doctor: “We’ll go through your concerns and decide the right next steps together.” Lower-left teal label over the laptop: “PLAN OF CARE: intelligent prescribing · summary · drug interactions · labs · referrals”.
pages.observation: The order is clear: header, three cards left to right, then the balloon, then the PLAN OF CARE label. Tier 1 is a product feature display with no story beat. The dentist, eye and paediatric specialties have nothing to do with Ravi's complaint of tiredness, which may make readers pause over why it is shown in his consultation. The doctor's line answers “I’ve been feeling tired lately” only generically. The Paediatrician card's lower edge runs past the screen onto the laptop bezel and keyboard area. The PLAN OF CARE label covers the laptop screen and the lower part of the doctor's white coat and right arm side, but not her face or gesturing hand. Ravi's shirt, watch and bag (on the floor at right) are consistent.

pages.scan: Tier 1 (wide panel): back at the front desk, the braided receptionist points at Ravi's phone as he leans on the counter, bag on his shoulder. Waiting patients are in the background. Balloon at top left, tail to the receptionist: “Welbuk Health is designed to help patients stay connected with their care.” Tier 2 left panel: Ravi holds up his phone showing a calendar and heart app, smiling. Balloon with tail to him: “So I can keep useful information in one place?” Lower-left teal label: “WELBUK HEALTH for patients”. Tier 2 right panel: the receptionist gestures toward Ravi, whose shoulder and phone are in the foreground at right. Balloon with tail down to her: “That’s the idea. Let’s walk through what is available to you.” Tier 3 (wide panel): caption “A smoother visit. A more connected experience.” Outside the clinic, the doctor and receptionist wave from the doorway as Ravi walks away waving, bag on his shoulder and phone in hand.
pages.observation: The scene jumps from the consultation room on page 6 to the front desk with no caption. Clothing and setting make it understandable, but the end of the consultation is skipped. The receptionist → Ravi → receptionist exchange is clear and well ordered, and Ravi's question gets a direct answer. The “WELBUK HEALTH for patients” label in tier 2 left sits right under Ravi's left hand and the bottom of the phone. It looks like it touches or slightly covers his lower fingers or the phone's base, so it should be checked. The receptionist's balloon tail in tier 1 is short and passes beside her face without covering it. Continuity is good: Ravi's sage shirt, brown bag, watch and phone; the receptionist's blue kurta, braid and bracelet; the doctor's white coat and teal kurta in tier 3.

pages.scan: Tier 1 left panel: caption “Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.” Ravi sits in a train or bus seat by a window, chin on hand, phone in his lap, bag on his shoulder. A city skyline is outside. Tier 1 right panel: top-left teal label “WELBUK VISION”. A new character, a grey-haired older doctor with glasses and a stethoscope, gestures at a modern clinic building, with dotted lines linking small houses in the sky. Bottom caption: “The vision: trusted connections between clinics, specialists, and patients across locations.” Tier 2 (wide panel): label “WELBUK VISION”, then caption “One connected ecosystem for care and family wellness.” Ravi sits on a sofa pointing at a tablet with person icons and a heart. It is held by a woman in a yellow kurta, with a smiling boy in an orange T-shirt leaning in. Tier 3 (wide panel): the receptionist (holding a phone), the doctor and Ravi (waving, bag on shoulder) stand in front of the clinic. Top-right teal label: “Welbuk Practice • Welbuk Care • Welbuk Health”. Bottom-left caption: “Welbuk — Building a connected healthcare ecosystem.”
pages.observation: There are several abrupt scene and time changes with no transition: the clinic exit to a train ride (“Tomorrow”), to a vision montage with an unintroduced older doctor, to a home scene, then back in front of the clinic. Whose voice the first caption is in is unclear. The “us” and “our hometown” in “Tomorrow, care may take us beyond our hometown.” could be Ravi's thought or a narrator. The older doctor, the woman in yellow and the boy are never named. Readers may assume the woman and boy are Ravi's wife and son, but nothing confirms it. The repeated “WELBUK VISION” label in tiers 1 and 2 signals that these are imagined or future scenes, which helps somewhat. Tier 3 has two text boxes in opposite corners. A reader would likely read the top-right product list first, then the bottom-left tagline. The product list uses “•” where earlier labels use “·”, a minor inconsistency. The bottom-left caption covers the hem and feet of the receptionist's kurta and comes close to the doctor's left leg and foot. The top-right label is near Ravi's head and raised hand but does not cover them. Ravi's sage shirt, watch and brown bag are consistent across all panels.
